title: The Fourier kernel and integrand
statement:
Let $p$ be a prime and let $\Lambda$ be a commutative ring in which $p$ is invertible. Let $\pi:V\to S$ and $\pi':V'\to S$ be morphisms of schemes [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions], and put $W=V\times_SV'$ [def-pc-fibre-product]. Assume $p=0$ in $\Gamma(W,\mathcal O_W)$; this condition allows $W$ to be empty. Fix a global function $b\in\Gamma(W,\mathcal O_W)$ (the pairing) and a group homomorphism $\Psi:(\mathbf F_p,+)\to\Lambda^\times$ (an additive character, allowed to be trivial).

Give $W$ its canonical $\mathbf F_p$-scheme structure: the ring map $\mathbf Z\to\Gamma(W,\mathcal O_W)$ factors through $\mathbf F_p=\mathbf Z/p\mathbf Z$, and this ring map determines the structure morphism $W\to\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf F_p$ by [lem-a1-locally-ringed-space-affine-adjunction]. View $b$ as the $\mathbf F_p$-morphism
$$
 \widetilde b:W\longrightarrow\mathbf A^1_{\mathbf F_p}=\operatorname{Spec}(\mathbf F_p[t])
$$
corresponding to the ring map $\mathbf F_p[t]\to\Gamma(W,\mathcal O_W)$ that sends $t$ to $b$, using [def-sbc-affine-space] and [lem-a1-locally-ringed-space-affine-adjunction].

Let $\mathcal L_\Psi$ be the Artin–Schreier sheaf on $\mathbf A^1_{\mathbf F_p}$ of [def-fd-artin-schreier-sheaf], using its current main-20261015 general-coefficient definition with $k=\mathbf F_p$ and $q=p$. The Fourier kernel is
$$
 \mathcal K_\psi:=\mathcal L_{\Psi,b}:=\widetilde b^*\mathcal L_\Psi
 \quad\text{in }\operatorname{Sh}(W_{\mathrm{\acute et}},\Lambda\text{-}\mathrm{Mod}).
$$
Here the small étale site is [def-weil-pbc-etale-site] and $\widetilde b^*$ is inverse image of sheaves with fixed coefficient ring [def-weil-pbc-inverse-image]. The notation $b^*\mathcal L_\Psi$ abbreviates $\widetilde b^*\mathcal L_\Psi$; the equality with $\mathcal L_{\Psi,b}$ is the definition of the Artin–Schreier sheaf of a function, not a further base-change assertion.

In the application, use the finite-field data $q=p^a$ and $k_0=\mathbf F_q$ of [def-fourier-set], $S=S_0$ is a separated scheme of finite type over $k_0$ (the conventions of [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions]), and $V=V_0\to S_0$ is a vector bundle of rank $r$ as in [def-asd-vector-bundle-zero-section]. Take $V'=V_0^\vee$, its dual vector bundle, with $b(x,\xi)=\langle x,\xi\rangle$. In local dual frames the pairing is $\sum_{i=1}^r x_i\xi_i$; the dual changes of coordinates are inverse transposes. For $S_0=\operatorname{Spec}k_0$, $V_0=\mathbf A^1_{k_0}$, this gives $b(x,\xi)=x\xi$ and the usual notation $\mathcal L_{\Psi,x\xi}$ for the kernel.

blueprint_update.statement:
Let $\Lambda$ be a commutative ring in which the prime $p$ is invertible,
let $\pi:V\to S$ and $\pi':V'\to S$ be morphisms of schemes such that
$V\times_SV'$ has characteristic $p$ (that is, $p=0$ in
$\Gamma(V\times_SV',\mathcal O)$), let
$b\in\Gamma(V\times_SV',\mathcal O)$ be a global function (the
*pairing*), and let $\Psi:(\mathbf F_p,+)\to\Lambda^\times$ be an
additive character. The *Fourier kernel* is the Artin–Schreier sheaf of
[def-fd-artin-schreier-sheaf], for $k=\mathbf F_p$, attached to $b$:

$$
\mathcal K_\psi:=\mathcal L_{\Psi,b}=b^*\mathcal L_\Psi ,
$$

a sheaf of $\Lambda$-modules on the small étale site of $V\times_SV'$,
where $b$ is viewed as a morphism $V\times_SV'\to\mathbf A^1_{\mathbf F_p}$.
In the application, $S=S_0$ is a separated scheme of finite type over
$k_0$ (conventions of [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions]), $V=V_0\to S_0$
is a vector bundle of rank $r$, $V'=V_0^\vee$ is its dual, and
$b(x,\xi)=\langle x,\xi\rangle$ is the evaluation pairing; on the affine
line over a field this is the sheaf $\mathcal L_{\psi(x\xi)}$.
